reason: Seawater can enter the seafloor through open fractures, starting the circulation loop.
expectation: Seawater will move down into the fractured rock.

effect: Seawater has entered the crust, so the next step is to heat it beneath the seafloor.
reaction: The circulation loop is beginning as expected.
reason: The infiltrating seawater can encounter the hot rock beneath the seafloor.
expectation: The seawater will heat up as it moves through the crust.

effect: The circulating seawater is now heated inside the crust; it can potentially rise back toward the sea.
reason: The heated water may rise through the open seafloor fractures, completing the circulation route.
expectation: The hot water will rise through the fractures toward the seafloor.

effect: The heated water reacts further with hot rock, becoming mineral-bearing hydrothermal fluid rather than rising directly through the fractures.
reaction: I was surprised that the failed attempt automatically revealed and performed the rock reaction.
reason: I expect the mineral-bearing fluid to return to the sea, but its available route is not yet clear.
expectation: The inspection should reveal what can bring the fluid back toward the sea.

effect: The mineral-bearing fluid is returning through fractures; it can now emerge into the sea.
reaction: The inspection clarified the return route and advanced it automatically.
reason: The returning hot fluid should meet the surrounding seawater at the vent.
expectation: The fluid will discharge into the sea and cool, potentially depositing minerals.

effect: The hot fluid mixed with cooler seawater, causing minerals to precipitate at the vent.
reaction: The mineral deposition followed as expected, though the goals are not yet marked complete.
reason: The precipitating minerals may be the next step toward building the vent deposit; their partner is not clear.
expectation: The inspection will reveal how the minerals can form a deposit.

effect: Precipitated minerals built a deposit around the outlet, completing the vent-deposit goal.
reaction: The modest deposit is a useful distinction from assuming every vent forms a tall chimney.
reason: The returning hot fluid still needs to enter the sea to complete the circulation loop.
expectation: The hydrothermal fluid will emerge into the sea.

effect: The returning fluid formed a hydrothermal plume, completing the circulation goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between suspended minerals and smoke was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following heated water as it reacted with rock, then cooled and deposited minerals, connected circulation to vent chemistry.

leastWorthwhile.text: The extra inspection after mineral precipitation felt less informative as a decision because its sole partner was automatically used.

surprise.text: Trying fractures before the water had reacted with rock instead revealed and automatically performed the rock reaction.

arbitrary.text: Using the fractures to build the deposit was not initially obvious, although the result explained that precipitation accumulated around an outlet.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see another natural process unfold, particularly if it connects physical circulation with chemistry as this chapter did.
